title: Volume 8 · The Service Desk: Issues, SLAs and Warranty Claims
subtitle: Lessons 1–10: logging issues against assets, running SLAs honestly, and settling warranty claims without losing money
outcomes: Log an issue against a serialised asset and keep the service history attached to it
Configure service levels that measure the response the client actually promised
Decide when a repair is free of charge and when it is billable, with evidence
Turn field service time into an invoice that matches the agreement

slides.title: Why service work needs its own document
bullets: A customer complaint is not a sales return, and treating it as one destroys the warranty history
An issue records who reported it, which asset, what the symptom was and who owns the fix
The same asset accumulates issues over years, which is how a client learns which model to stop buying
Without an issue record, the service team keeps its history in a chat group and the warranty claim in a memory
A distributor with an assembly line needs this even at two issues a week

rows: Issue exists as its own document
Issue linked to a serialised asset

slides.notes: The first objection is always volume: we only get two complaints a week. Volume is not the argument, warranty is. Without a per-asset history, the client cannot tell an early failure from a misuse pattern, and pays for both.

slides.title: A five-field issue that survives an audit
bullets: Asset, symptom, reporter, priority and promised response: five fields, filled every time
The symptom is written in the customer's words plus one sentence of technical description
Priority is set by impact, not by who shouted, and the SLA clock follows the priority
Attach the photograph at logging time, because the second visit is where the cost is
Nothing is closed without a resolution note a stranger could understand

rows: Open Issue for customer Kim Huat Hardware
Write the symptom in the customer's words
Attach the photograph and a reading

slides.notes: Five fields, consistently, is worth more than twenty fields filled sometimes. The photograph at logging is the highest-value habit, because it turns a second site visit into a phone call.

slides.title: Make the SLA measurable or do not promise it
bullets: A service level is a response and a resolution target per priority, not an aspiration in a proposal
Response means the clock stops when someone with the right skill starts, not when the ticket is read
Holiday calendars and working hours belong in the setup, or the SLA breaches itself over a long weekend
Measure from submission to first response, and report the breaches with their cause
A client who signs an eight-hour promise with no weekend cover has bought a number they cannot meet

rows: Set working hours and holidays for the service calendar
Raise a test issue outside working hours
Clock counts from the next working hour
Respond and check the elapsed time

slides.notes: Most SLA failures are calendar failures, not people failures. A promise of four hours starting at five on Friday means the clock runs all weekend unless the calendar says otherwise. Configure it, then demonstrate the weekend test.

slides.title: What an SLA report must prove
bullets: The elapsed time must be computed from stored timestamps, not from a note in the description
A breach must be attributable: which target, which priority, which agent, which cause
Response and resolution are separate measures, and a fast response with a slow resolution is still a breach
Report the median and the worst case, because the average hides the customer who is about to leave
Keep the report small enough that the service lead reads it weekly
slides.notes: An SLA report that says ninety-eight per cent is useless if the two per cent are the client's biggest account. Show the worst case next to the median, and make the review weekly so the breach is a conversation rather than a post-mortem.

slides.title: The warranty decision, with evidence
bullets: Warranty is a date, a serial and a condition, and all three must be findable in one place
The delivery date of the serial is the warranty start, not the invoice date of the first order from that customer
Free of charge covers the part and the labour per the agreement, and the agreement must say which
Damage in transit and misuse are exclusions, and the photograph taken at logging is what settles the argument
Record the decision with the reason, because next year's claim will refer to this one

rows: Free of charge, yes or no, with reason
Parts and labour on a quotation

slides.notes: The warranty decision is where a distributor leaks money quietly, usually by goodwill. Goodwill is a fine policy if it is recorded and limited, and a disaster if it is assumed. Make the decision explicit and store the reason.

slides.title: Three outcomes and the documents each needs
bullets: A repair consumes parts and labour, which is a material issue and a service invoice
A replacement ships a new serial and takes the old one back, which is a delivery and a return, never a deletion
A credit closes the commercial complaint, and only where the goods are not coming back
Each outcome creates a different document trail, so the choice is made before the work, not after
Never re-use a serial number for a replacement unit

rows: Decide the outcome with the customer
Issue the parts to the job
For a replacement, despatched and received back
Close the issue with the resolution note

slides.notes: The replacement path is the one that goes wrong, because someone ships a new unit and forgets the return, so the old serial stays in stock forever. Decide the outcome first and let the documents follow it.

slides.title: Time, travel and the invoice that follows
bullets: Field time is billable or absorbed by the agreement, and either way it is recorded per issue
Travel is a line item the client signed for, not a surprise at month end
Time recorded in a chat message is not evidence; it belongs on the document it bills against
A service invoice that does not name the issue cannot be defended when the customer queries it
Batch the invoicing monthly, but record the time the day it happens

rows: Record the visit against the issue
Add travel as a separate line
Check the agreement for what is included
Generate the invoice for the month
Attach the visit log to the invoice

slides.notes: Clients query service invoices more than any other kind, because the work is invisible after it is done. A line that names the issue, the date and the technician ends the query before it starts.

slides.title: What the serial number accumulates
bullets: The serial number is the thread: delivery, warranty start, issues, parts consumed, invoices
Two years of history answers the question the client asks next year: is this model worth buying again
Failure rate per model is a purchasing input, not a service statistic
A repair that consumes parts should show on the asset, so the next technician knows what was replaced
Report the top ten failing serials quarterly, and expect that report to change a purchasing decision

rows: Every issue attached to a serial
Top ten serials by issue count

slides.notes: This is the commercial argument for the whole chapter. A distributor who can show that one model generates three times the warranty cost has a purchasing decision for free. Build the ranking once and the client will maintain it.

slides.title: Four numbers the service lead should trust
bullets: Open issues by priority, because that is the queue somebody has to work today
Median response and median resolution, split by priority rather than averaged across all
Warranty cost as a percentage of the model's revenue, which is the number purchasing reacts to
Billable versus absorbed hours, because absorbed hours are a decision and should be seen as one
If a number cannot be produced from the documents, it is not a metric, it is an opinion
slides.notes: Four numbers, weekly, beats a dashboard nobody opens. The test for each is the same: can it be produced from the documents alone? If a spreadsheet is needed, the process has a hole worth fixing.

slides.title: The service playbook
bullets: One page per scenario: log, respond, decide warranty, repair or replace, invoice, close
The warranty rules in writing, with the exclusions the client actually intends to enforce
The escalation path with names and hours, because an SLA without escalation is a wish
The monthly pack: the four numbers, the breach list and the warranty ranking
The parts list a technician is allowed to consume without approval

rows: Log, respond, decide, repair, invoice, close

slides.notes: Close with the playbook, because the desk outlives the project. The parts authority limit is the line most often missing: without it a technician either waits for approval on a bearing or consumes a motor unasked, and both cost money.

lab.title: Lab · Run one warranty claim end to end at Seri Murni
steps: Open an issue against serial SN-2026-00418 with a photograph and a reading attached
Set the priority, confirm the SLA clock started, and record the calendar it is measured against
Raise a second test issue outside working hours and check when its clock begins
Look up the serial's delivery date and state whether the claim is inside the warranty period
Decide repair, replacement or credit, and write the reason into the resolution note
Issue the parts and book the technician's two and a half hours against the issue
Raise the invoice with parts, labour, travel and service tax, naming the issue on every line
Produce the four service numbers and the breach list, and add them to the monthly pack
lab.done: One issue closed with a defensible warranty decision, its parts and time consumed against the asset, an invoice that names the issue, and four service numbers produced from documents alone.

quiz.question: Why must a service complaint be logged as an issue rather than a sales return?
options: Because the issue keeps the per-asset history that the warranty decision depends on
Because issues are cheaper to process
quiz.why: A return records goods movement. The issue records symptom, reporter and asset, which is what tells you whether a failure is inside warranty and whether a model is worth buying again.

quiz.question: What makes an SLA meetable rather than aspirational?
options: Working hours and holidays configured, with response measured from stored timestamps
quiz.why: Most breaches are calendar breaches. Without working hours the clock runs through nights and weekends, and without timestamps the measurement is somebody's recollection.

quiz.question: When does a serial number's warranty period start?
options: When the item was purchased from the supplier
When the serialised unit was delivered to the customer
When the first issue is raised
quiz.why: Delivery of the specific serial is the only date that matches the unit in the customer's hands. Using the supplier's purchase date shortens the warranty the customer was promised.

quiz.question: What is the dangerous omission in a replacement rather than a repair?
options: Failing to raise a service invoice
Shipping the new serial without receiving the old one back
quiz.why: The old unit stays in stock forever and the ledger keeps an asset that no longer exists. Replacement needs a delivery out and a return in, both visible.

quiz.question: Which service figure is most likely to change a purchasing decision?
options: Warranty cost as a percentage of revenue per model
quiz.why: It joins service cost to the commercial result for a specific model, which is the comparison a purchasing manager can act on. The others manage today's queue.

memory.spine: Log the issue against the serial, measure the clock, decide warranty with evidence, and bill what the agreement allows.

device.label: Priority before promise
expansion: Priority is set by impact at logging, and the SLA clock follows the priority
Promises are made in a calendar, so working hours and holidays decide the measurement
Warranty is decided from the serial's delivery date and recorded with its reason
Repair, replace or credit is chosen before work starts, because each needs different documents
Every closed issue carries a resolution note and, if billable, an invoice that names it

cards.q: Which five fields make an issue defensible later?
cards.a: Asset, symptom, reporter, priority and promised response, plus the resolution note on close. Everything else is optional.

cards.q: Why do service levels breach themselves over a long weekend?
cards.a: Because the clock runs on the service calendar. If working hours and holidays are not configured, a Friday evening issue breaches by Monday morning.

cards.q: What decides whether a repair is free of charge?
cards.a: The serial's delivery date against the warranty period, the exclusions in the agreement, and the evidence attached at logging. The decision and its reason are recorded.

cards.q: Why is a replacement the riskiest of the three service outcomes?
cards.a: Because it needs a delivery out and the old unit back in. If the return is forgotten, a serial that no longer exists stays in stock forever.

cards.q: Which four numbers belong in the monthly service pack?
cards.a: Open issues by priority, median response and resolution per priority, warranty cost versus revenue per model, and billable versus absorbed hours.

trap.what: The client handles complaints by phone and goodwill, so the desk is configured but never used, and warranty cost is invisible.
trap.why: Goodwill with no record is a subsidy nobody measures. Log every complaint against the serial, record each warranty decision with its reason, and put the four numbers in a monthly pack the purchasing lead reads.

narration: Service work is where a distributor leaks money without noticing, and it starts with the document. A complaint is not a sales return: it is an issue, logged against a serial number, in the customer's words, with a photograph and an owner. Priority comes from impact, and the service level clock follows the priority, which is why working hours and holidays must be configured before anyone promises four hours on a Friday. Warranty is a date, a serial and a condition. Find the delivery date of that exact unit, check the exclusions, and record the decision with its reason, because next year's claim will refer to this one. Then choose the outcome before the work starts: a repair consumes parts and time, a replacement ships a new serial and must take the old one back, a credit closes the commercial complaint. Bill from the issue, so every line names the asset and the visit. And finish with the four numbers the service lead should trust: open issues by priority, median response and resolution, warranty cost against revenue per model, and billable against absorbed hours.
